full_judgment:
Mohammad Imman Ali, J. This Civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 23.04.2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1036 of 2007 discharging the Rule. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent No. 1 as plaintiffs instituted suit for declaration of his title in the land in dispute claiming that .72 acre of land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 228, plot No. 123 of Mouza Kashinagar, under Police Station-Nandail, District-Mymensingh belonged to Barkot Mondol of which the C.S. Record was prepared in the name of his son Ekdil Mondol. The S.A. Record in respect of the said land was prepared in the name of Abdul Aziz, Hafiz Uddin and Shahed Ali. After death of S.A. recorded tenant Shahed Ali his son Bacchu Miah sold .02 acre of land of disputed plot No. 125 to the plaintiff by executing a kabala dated 04.04.2001. Former Zaminder Gyanda Sundari Chowdhury, the C.S. recorded Malik as its owner and possessor settled .01 acre out of .88 acre of land of disputed plot No. 124 with the plaintiff and his brother whereon they have been running their business by constructing huts. The said .01 acre settled with them was recorded in their names in S.A. Khatian No. 222, one Yousuf Ali also took settlement of .02 acre of plot No. 124 from the said Zaminder and while he had been in enjoyment and possession sold the same to the plaintiff by executing a kabala dated 06.07.1960 before preparation of the S.A. record which was wrongly prepared in the name of Yousuf Ali. In such manner he (plaintiff) has been enjoying and possessing .02 acre in plot No. 125 and .01 1/2 acre in plot No. 124, in total .03 1/2 acre, and it was mutated in his name and he has been enjoying and possessing the same paying rent to the Government. Out of .88 acre of land of plot No. 124, .82 acre was wrongly recorded in Khas Khatian No. 1 and the remaining .06 acre was recorded in the names of different persons including him. The land of disputed plot No. 124 is situated in Khaligonj Bazar. There is a Mahogany Tree in his land in plot No. 125 and in the same plot the Kaligonj Jame Masjid is situated. For renovation of his huts he used a branch of his said tree and at that time the surveyor of local land office demanded bribe from him. Being refused, the surveyor instituted a false criminal case against him and others. Earlier he filed other class Suit No. 97 of 2002 in respect of the same land, but for some formal defects that suit was withdrawn with permission to sue afresh. The defendants threatened to dispossess him from the suit land on 21.12.2002. 

 2. The defendant Government contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations claiming that .82 acre of land out of .88 acre in plot No. 124 was recorded in Khatian No. 1 and the record in respect of the remaining .06 acre was prepared in the names of different persons namely Abdul Hamid and Moqbul Hossain in respect of .02 acre in Khatian No. 219, Abdul Hafiz in respect of .02 acre in Khatian No. 212, Yousuf Ali in respect of .01 acre in Khatian No. 220, Besides that S.A. Khatian No. 220 in respect of .44 acre of disputed plot No. 125 was prepared in the name of Abdul Aziz, S.A. Khatian No. 227 in respect of .20 acre of disputed plot No. 125 was prepared in the name of Ismail, S.A. Khatian No. 230 in respect of .04 acre of plot No. 125 was prepared in the name of Akhter Hussain on behalf of the Mosque and S.A. Khatian No. 231 in respect of .04 acre of land of plot No. 125 was prepared in the name of Aftab Ali. As per the Government policy the plaintiff was evicted from the suit land by demolishing his huts thereon. In .82 acre of land of plot No. 124 the Union Land Office is situated Earlier on the plaintiff instituted another suit in respect of the same land and finding no scope of success withdrew that suit and instituted the instant suit with false claim which is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. The High Court Division found that plaintiffs land was specifically disclosed in the plaint mentioning the plot numbers. Khatian numbers and quantum of land giving boundary and sketch map stating the manner of possession. The High Court Division also noted that the Government claim chat the suit land became Khas under the Government was not supported by any proof of transmission of ownership from the former landlord to the Government.
